uncited: Shadow Volume Mipmap Generation creates a multiresolution hierarchy for 3D shadow volume textures to enable efficient rendering at varying distances or resolutions.

It solves the problem of preserving shadow presence information during downsampling by using bitwise OR accumulation, ensuring that if any voxel in a parent block is shadowed, the corresponding voxel in the child block remains shadowed.

This method is distinct from [Atlas Mipmapping](2639-atlas-mipmapping.md) which handles 2D texture atlases, [Voxel Pre-integration](2956-voxel-pre-integration.md) which averages density, and [GPU 3D Mip Chain Generation](5067-gpu-3d-mip-chain-generation.md) which typically uses fragment shaders for downsampling; this method is a CPU-side bitwise accumulation approach.
Dimensions are `width_mip0`, `height_mip0`, `depth_mip0`.
- `width_mip0`, `height_mip0`, `depth_mip0`: Integer dimensions of the base level.
- A 3-level mipmap chain (`mip0`, `mip1`, `mip2`) uploaded to a 3D OpenGL texture.
- All `uint8_t` values are 0 (unshadowed) or 1 (shadowed).
Allocate `shadow_volume_mip1` of size `volume_mip1` bytes.
Iterate $x$ from 0 to $width_{mip0}-1$, $y$ from 0 to $height_{mip0}-1$, $z$ from 0 to $depth_{mip0}-1$.
Allocate `shadow_volume_mip2` of size `volume_mip2` bytes.
Iterate $x$ from 0 to $width_{mip1}-1$, $y$ from 0 to $height_{mip1}-1$, $z$ from 0 to $depth_{mip1}-1$.
Set `glPixelStorei(GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 1)`.
Upload `mip0` using `glTexSubImage3D` with format `GL_RED_INTEGER`, type `GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE`, and data `shadow_volume_mip0`.
Upload `mip1` using `glTexSubImage3D` with format `GL_RED_INTEGER`, type `GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE`, and data `shadow_volume_mip1`.
Upload `mip2` using `glTexSubImage3D` with format `GL_RED_INTEGER`, type `GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE`, and data `shadow_volume_mip2`.
Free memory for `shadow_volume_mip1` and `shadow_volume_mip2`.
The downsampling factor is always 2 per dimension.
- **Edge Cases:** If any dimension of the input is less than 2, the corresponding mip level dimension becomes 0, and the loop for that level will not execute.
The bitwise OR operation ensures that shadow presence is never lost, but detail is reduced.
Boundary conditions are handled by the integer division which effectively maps 4 parent voxels to 1 child voxel.
- **Bitwise OR Accumulation:** A downsampling technique where child values are the logical OR of parent values.
It is chosen when binary presence/absence (like shadowing) must be preserved across resolutions.
It differs from averaging (used in density mips) by being non-destructive to presence. [Bitwise OR Mipmap Accumulation](2602-mipmap-generation.md#subtopics)
- **3D Texture Mipmapping:** The process of generating lower-resolution versions of a 3D texture.
This method is specific to shadow volumes, whereas general 3D mipmapping might use different filtering. [GPU 3D Mip Chain Generation](5067-gpu-3d-mip-chain-generation.md)
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of voxels in the base level, as each voxel is visited a constant number of times (once for mip1, once for mip2).
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ for storing the mipmap chain.
The total memory is $N + N/8 + N/64 \approx 1.14N$ bytes.
- **Measured Performance:** Not given in the sources.
- **Limitations:** Only generates 3 levels; requires CPU processing; not suitable for dynamic volumes without regeneration.
- **When to use:** Static shadow volumes where CPU preprocessing is acceptable.
- **When not to use:** Dynamic scenes requiring real-time mipmap generation; scenes requiring more than 3 levels.
It is used in voxel-based rendering systems to optimize shadow volume rendering by using lower-resolution shadow volumes for distant or less critical areas.
